finding: A concrete UTC-day rollover gap exists in the public accounting owner. ModelAdmission currently stops listing a denied row once its utc_day is no longer today, and resumePending returns CONFLICT for that row. The owned fake clock and fixed external quota observation seam can reach this behavior through the existing AT-ops-10 probe and disposable PostgreSQL stack without authenticated provider access, root, new infrastructure, or R1 activation. A proper retry must create a current-day attempt and leave the original accounting day and bindings immutable; clock advancement alone cannot prove a quota reset.

requirements: Persist the denied attempt and reset information.
Mark the current review slot deferred_quota.
Preserve the obligation and cumulative budget.
Schedule a bounded retry after reset, respecting provider retry timing.
Resume only after a fresh successful usage/admission check.

cadenceBoundary.limitation: The current floor defers a scheduled slot inside its 180-second window and admits an unbound scheduled slot. It does not re-admit a deferred slot after a reset. This accounting case must not claim canonical cadence slot/wake dispatch or a production native schedule anchor.

steps: At 23:59 UTC, create the existing denied, uncharged pending call with a normalized exhausted observation whose reset is 00:05 UTC on the next date. Retain its public readback.

Restart the owned disposable PostgreSQL fixture as the existing phase already does, then advance the existing fake clock to 00:02 UTC. Call resumePending for the old call key while the latest provider observation remains exhausted.
Assert the old call is not admitted or charged from clock advancement alone; its original utc_day and binding remain unchanged and the pending work remains readable.
Advance the fake clock past 00:05 UTC, record a fresh authorized normalized available observation through the existing provider seam, then call resumePending for the pending work.

Assert the returned attempt is on the new UTC day, has a new call ID, preserves account, root/budget group, run, generation, route and work class, and is visible through the public pending/owner readback as appropriate. Repeat the resume/readback to prove idempotency and one current-day charge.
observableAssertions: Original denied record retains its original UTC day and uncharged decision; it is never re-dated or rebound.
An exhausted observation before reset leaves the attempt denied/uncharged, even after midnight.
Only the fresh available observation after reset permits a current-day reservation; the same logical run and cumulative budget group are preserved.
The reservation is charged at most once to the new UTC-day count.
No native provider request occurs: nativeSendCount is zero, providerSendPermitIssued is false, and paidRequests is zero.
